How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (6)

  1. In what year was Feedzai founded, and under which legal entity?
    Company age is an input to maturity and viability assessment.
  2. How many full-time employees does Feedzai have, and how many work in engineering and customer support?
    Headcount indicates capacity to support a large bank deployment.
  3. How much equity funding has Feedzai raised in total, and from whom?
    Total capital raised is an input to judging financial resilience.
  4. Has Feedzai had any security incident affecting customer data or service in the last five years, and how was each disclosed?
    A bank needs the vendor's security incident record before sending it customer data.
  5. Which financial-institution customers have ended their use of Feedzai in the last three years, and why?
    Loss of large customers can signal product or service problems.
  6. Have there been any unplanned executive departures or conduct findings at Feedzai in the last three years?
    Leadership instability or conduct issues affect vendor reliability.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-12 · launch Feedzai
    Feedzai expands Digital Trust to detect AI agents accessing bank accounts

    Feedzai announced in a press release dated 12 November 2026 that it has expanded its Digital Trust solution so banks can detect AI agents signing in to customer accounts. The release describes persistent device fingerprinting, a risk score drawing on shared intelligence, and cryptographic device binding that can also serve as a possession factor in place of SMS one-time passcodes. It states no availability date or pricing, and the performance figures in it are Feedzai's own. Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-11-10 · leadership change Feedzai
    Feedzai appoints Joost van Mook as chief revenue officer

    Feedzai's press-release index lists a release dated 2026-11-10 announcing Joost van Mook as chief revenue officer; the leadership page shows him in that role. Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-09-24 · launch Feedzai
    Feedzai launches Farol, an AI agent embedded in RiskOps Studio

    Feedzai announced Farol, an AI agent inside RiskOps Studio that summarises alerts, analyses rule performance, answers product questions and helps draft suspicious activity reports. The release does not name the underlying model providers. Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-06-09 · launch Feedzai
    Feedzai makes Feedzai IQ Score available, including on AWS Marketplace

    Feedzai announced availability of Feedzai IQ Score, a fraud risk score delivered by API and derived from signals across its customer network using what it describes as federated learning that shares aggregated, anonymised risk signals rather than raw customer data. The release says the score is available on AWS Marketplace. Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  5. 2025-10-02 · funding Feedzai
    Feedzai announces about US$75M round at US$2B valuation and ECB digital euro selection

    Feedzai announced a new investment round of about US$75 million at a stated US$2 billion valuation, naming Lince Capital, Iberis Capital and Explorer Investments as new investors and Oxy Capital and Buenavista Equity Partners as returning ones. In the same release it said the European Central Bank had selected it, with PwC as subcontractor, under a framework agreement for digital euro fraud and risk management with an estimated value of EUR 79.1 million and a maximum of EUR 237.3 million. Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  6. 2025-04-22 · acquisition Feedzai
    Feedzai acquires Demyst and its Zonic data orchestration platform

    Feedzai announced the acquisition of Demyst, including its Zonic data workflow orchestration platform and data-integration capabilities. Terms were not disclosed. Demyst's chief executive and key staff were to join Feedzai. Feedzai (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)
